positioning.known_upper_point: The published 8xMI355X 288-GiB TP8 configuration fits approximately 205.401 GiB per rank before unmodeled runtime overhead.
positioning.question_not_assumption: HBF may make lower-HBM ranks capacity-feasible; the study must separately determine whether memory service remains feasible.
positioning.simulator_role: adjudicate capacity, traffic, latency hiding, tier contention, and physical flash writes under one byte-identical contract

questions.question: At fixed TP8 compute, can HBM+HBF make Kimi K3 capacity- and memory-service-feasible on 192-GiB or 96-GiB HBM ranks, and where is the capacity-enough/bandwidth-insufficient boundary?
questions.answer_rule: Classify capacity fit independently from modeled memory service. Among byte-identical capacity-feasible points, report offered-to-completion latency and makespan without calling any point deployable until compute and communication timing are calibrated.
questions.negative_result_is_valid: HBF can satisfy capacity while failing to provide enough service bandwidth or latency hiding.

questions.question: For 896-expert top-16 Kimi K3, when should selected cold experts be read directly from HBF and when should they be prefetched into HBM double buffers?
questions.required_evidence: token-and-layer Kimi K3 router activations from real weights; synthetic routing is sensitivity-only
questions.answer_rule: For each identical token, layer, and router window, report direct access and HBM staging as a Pareto comparison over offered latency, makespan, extra HBM traffic, and HBF traffic. Declare no universal winner when the crossover depends on expert union, locality, or lookahead.
questions.negative_result_is_valid: No static hot set or prefetch policy dominates direct reads across realistic routing windows.

questions.question: Can HBF beneficially hold any mutable 1M-context Kimi K3 MLA/KDA or prefix state, or should HBF remain a read-only weight tier?
questions.answer_rule: Keep the mutable-state lifecycle byte-identical across placements and report latency together with logical and physical writes. A read-only run has null WAF; no HBF benefit may omit its physical-write cost or rely on an unreported lifetime model.
questions.negative_result_is_valid: KV/state latency or physical writes make writable DRAM/CXL preferable despite HBF capacity.
